common_name: Kissproof Daffodil (Large-Cupped Daffodil with Orange-Red Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Kissproof is a large-cupped daffodil with greenish-yellow petals and a vivid reddish-orange cup.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Kissproof is a Division 2 large-cupped daffodil hybridized by Warnaar and Co. of the Netherlands, registered in 1964, bearing a single flower per stem with soft greenish-yellow petals surrounding a bold, flared cup in a saturated reddish-orange that holds its color well as the bloom ages. It is a mid-season bloomer with sturdy stems suited to borders and cutting. Allow the foliage to die back naturally after bloom, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply.

common_name: Pinza Daffodil (Large-Cupped Daffodil with Orange-Banded Cup)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Pinza is a Richardson-bred large-cupped daffodil with deep yellow petals and a cup rimmed in a broad band of orange.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Pinza is a Division 2 large-cupped daffodil bred by J. Lionel Richardson as part of his Race Horse series, registered in 1962, with clear deep yellow petals and a flared, slightly flanged cup that shades from orangey-yellow at the base into a broad orange band at the rim. It is a vigorous, long-lasting mid-season bloomer that earned recognition from the Royal Horticultural Society for its garden performance. Allow the foliage to die back naturally after bloom, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Obdam is a late-blooming double daffodil with fully double, ivory-white flowers.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Obdam is a Division 4 double daffodil bearing fully double, creamy ivory-white blooms with a tightly packed, rose-like center rather than a distinct trumpet, flowering later in the season than most doubles. Its sturdy stems make it a reliable choice for borders and cutting gardens. Allow the foliage to die back naturally after bloom, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun; Ice King is a double sport of Ice Follies, introduced in 1984, with ruffled lemon-yellow petals that fade to creamy white.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Ice King is a Division 4 double daffodil that arose as a sport of the popular 'Ice Follies' and was introduced in 1984, producing large, fully double, carnation-like blooms with ruffled lemon-yellow petals that gradually fade to creamy white as the flower matures. It blooms in mid-spring on sturdy stems and makes a long-lasting cut flower. Allow the foliage to die back naturally after bloom, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Papillon Blanc is a split-corona daffodil with pure white petals and a frilly, butterfly-like corona touched with pale yellow and peach.

directions: Plant bulbs about 6 inches deep and 6 inches apart in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade in fall. Papillon Blanc is a Division 11 split-corona daffodil whose corona segments are split for more than half their length and splayed flat against the white petals, giving each flower a frilled, butterfly-like look touched with pale yellow, peach, and primrose that fades toward white as the bloom ages. It flowers in mid to late spring and makes an unusual, long-lasting cut flower. Allow the foliage to die back naturally after bloom, and leave established clumps undisturbed to multiply.

common_name: Ivory Floradale Tulip (Ivory Darwin Hybrid Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Ivory Floradale is an ivory-white sport of the Darwin hybrid tulip 'Floradale', registered in 1965.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Ivory Floradale, a sport of the Darwin hybrid 'Floradale' registered in 1965, produces enormous blooms that open creamy yellow and brighten to ivory-white as they mature, occasionally showing faint carmine flecking on the outer petals. Like other Darwin hybrids it has sturdy, wind-resistant stems and tends to perennialize better than many tulip types in climates with sufficient winter chill. Deadhead after bloom and allow foliage to yellow naturally before removing it.

common_name: Gavota Tulip (Burgundy Triumph Tulip Edged in Gold)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Gavota is a Triumph tulip with deep burgundy-maroon petals dramatically edged in golden yellow.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Gavota is a Triumph-class tulip bearing deep burgundy-maroon, egg-shaped blooms with a distinctive, irregular band of golden yellow along each petal edge, giving a striking two-tone effect that holds up well in mid-spring weather. Its sturdy, medium-height stems make it a reliable choice for beds, containers, and cutting. In mild-winter areas without adequate chill, treat as an annual rather than expecting it to perennialize.

common_name: Design Impression Tulip (Variegated-Leaf Darwin Hybrid Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Design Impression is a Darwin hybrid tulip with variegated foliage and large rose-colored blooms flushed gold.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Design Impression is a Darwin hybrid tulip from the Impression series, notable for deep green leaves edged in a narrow lime-yellow margin that make the plant ornamental even before bloom; its large flowers open a radiant rose color with a muted golden flush at the base. The sturdy, tall stems resist wind and rain better than many other tulip classes. Allow foliage to yellow and die back naturally after flowering to build reserves for the following year.

common_name: Texas Flame Tulip (Yellow Parrot Tulip Flamed Scarlet)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Texas Flame is a classic parrot tulip with buttercup-yellow petals boldly flamed in scarlet-red.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall, siting plants where they are sheltered from strong wind since the large, ruffled blooms are heavy. Texas Flame is a long-grown parrot tulip with buttercup-yellow petals dramatically flamed in scarlet-red and touched with green at the base, the wildly curled and fringed edges becoming more pronounced as each bloom opens and ages. It flowers in late spring and is a dramatic addition to borders or cut arrangements. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: Weber's Parrot Tulip (Large Pastel Parrot Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Weber's Parrot bears oversized creamy-white blooms flushed with green and soft pink.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in a sheltered, full-sun spot in fall, since the oversized blooms benefit from protection from wind and heavy rain. Weber's Parrot is one of the largest parrot tulips, with creamy-white petals flushed green and soft pink and an irregular, feathered texture along the frayed edges that gives each flower a painterly, almost ragged look. It flowers mid to late spring and works well as a striking cut flower. Deadhead after bloom and let the foliage die back naturally to recharge the bulb.

common_name: Orange Favourite Tulip (Fragrant Orange Parrot Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Orange Favourite is a historic, fragrant parrot tulip introduced in 1930.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Orange Favourite is a historic parrot tulip introduced in 1930, bearing richly ruffled orange petals streaked with green at the base and carrying a distinctive sweet, jasmine-like fragrance rare among tulips. It blooms in late spring on medium-height stems and has remained popular for nearly a century for both bedding and cutting. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Fringed Elegance is an RHS Award of Garden Merit fringed tulip with primrose-yellow petals edged in fine crystalline fringe.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Fringed Elegance bears primrose-yellow blooms that pale toward the petal tips, each edge finished in a delicate, crystalline fringe that catches the light and distinguishes the fringed tulip class from smooth-edged types. It flowers in late spring on tall, sturdy stems and earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: Huis Ten Bosch Tulip (Rose Pink Fringed Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Huis Ten Bosch is a fringed tulip with magenta-pink, cup-shaped blooms edged in fine white fringe.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Huis Ten Bosch is a late-flowering fringed tulip bearing cup-shaped blooms in rich magenta-pink over a creamy-white base, each petal trimmed with a delicate, lacy white fringe that catches the light. It reaches a good height for mid-border plantings and pairs well with other late-season fringed and lily-flowered tulips. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Esperanto is a viridiflora tulip with cream-edged variegated leaves and red-and-pink petals streaked with green.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Esperanto is a naturally occurring viridiflora sport of the tulip 'Hollywood', raised in 1968 by J. Spranger, grown as much for its light green leaves edged in creamy white as for its flowers, which open deep scarlet-red and age to soft pink and white with a broad central green flame on each petal. It is one of the shorter viridiflora types and flowers late in the tulip season, lending itself well to containers and the front of borders. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: Black Hero Tulip (Double Late Maroon-Black Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Black Hero is a double late tulip sport of 'Queen of the Night' with fully double, maroon-black blooms.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Black Hero is a double late (peony-flowered) sport of the classic heirloom 'Queen of the Night', its layered petals a deep midnight maroon that reads nearly black in shade and glistens burgundy in direct sun; the fully double blooms can open to several inches across, resembling a peony. It flowers late in the tulip season on sturdy stems and makes a dramatic contrast planted with pale or citrus-colored companions. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: La Belle Epoque Tulip (Apricot Double Late Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; La Belle Epoque is a double late tulip with large, peony-like blooms in antique apricot, salmon, and caramel tones.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. La Belle Epoque is a double late (peony-flowered) tulip introduced in the early 2000s, prized for its large, fully double blooms in shifting antique tones of salmon-apricot, butterscotch, and cream that pale further as each flower matures. Its sturdy stems and unusual, old-fashioned coloring have made it a favorite among cut-flower growers, though supply has historically been limited. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: Sugar Crystal Tulip (Pink Fringed Double Late Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Sugar Crystal is a double late tulip with soft pink, fully double blooms edged in a fine fringed margin.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun in fall. Sugar Crystal combines the fully double, peony-like form of the double late class with the trimmed petal edges of a fringed tulip, its soft pink petals blending into deeper rose tones and finished with a fine, crystalline fringe that turns silvery as the bloom matures. It flowers late in the tulip season and makes a long-lasting, textural cut flower. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Maytime is a 1942-introduced lily-flowered tulip with magenta-purple petals finely edged in white.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in a wind-sheltered, full-sun spot in fall. Maytime is a long-grown lily-flowered tulip, introduced in 1942, with slender, pointed petals that deepen to purple-magenta at the base and fade through lilac to a fine white edge, opening around a yellow center. Its graceful, waisted form and strong stems make it a good choice for borders and arrangements, flowering toward the end of the tulip season. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.

common_name: Marilyn Tulip (White Lily-Flowered Tulip Flamed Red)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Marilyn is a lily-flowered tulip with ivory-white petals flamed in strawberry red.

directions: Plant bulbs six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil in a wind-sheltered, full-sun spot in fall. Marilyn is a Rembrandt-style lily-flowered tulip whose pointed, recurving petals are ivory-white, irregularly flamed and streaked with strawberry-red in a bold, painterly pattern that varies somewhat from bloom to bloom. It flowers mid to late spring on tall stems well suited to the middle or back of a border, and the graphic color contrast makes it a standout cut flower. Allow foliage to die back naturally after bloom before removing it.
